items.title: French cities calm overnight after curfews imposed to quell violence, PM says
items.description: Sébastien Lecornu said new curfews for Tuesday night would be decided where necessary.

items.title: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC
items.description: Serhii Beskrestnov says there has not been enough time to warn people about incoming missile attacks. The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing.

items.title: Seventh day of violent clashes between Albanian protesters and police
items.description: Almost 300 people have been injured, more than half of them police, as violent anti-government demonstrations show no sign of easing.

items.title: Canadian tourist found guilty of animal cruelty after stealing Las Vegas flamingo from enclosure
items.description: The man testified that he snatched Peachy from its enclosure at the Flamingo hotel and casino after drinking 30 to 40 beers, but did not mean any harm.

items.title: Mission blasts off for Mars to grab a piece of its moon
items.description: A spacecraft is set to launch on an ambitious mission to bring 10g of Martian moon dust back to Earth.

items.title: Kenya cult leader who told parents to starve children guilty of 191 murders
items.description: Self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie was found guilty of 191 murder charges - all but one of them children.

items.title: Tennis star Svitolina says emotional toll of Ukraine war led to Monfils separation
items.description: The two top tennis pros married in 2021 and have one child together.

items.title: Vinted blocks French looters listing stolen goods for sale
items.description: The platform said since the weekend it had "taken immediate action to idenitify and remove listings linked to looting".

items.title: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of planting device had Saudi support, says court filing
items.description: The Saudi government did not immediately respond to BBC requests for comment.

items.title: Exiled critic of Rwandan president found beheaded
items.description: Former army sergeant major Robert Kabera was a popular YouTuber and singer, who had sought asylum in Uganda.

items.title: Houthi missile strike on Yemen camp kills 50 security recruits, local authorities say
items.description: Three missiles hit a camp in government-controlled Shabwa province that officials say was being used as a training centre for new recruits.

items.title: Obama blasts federal probe of Ilhan Omar as 'so appalling'
items.description: Obama says federal agents' search of the Democrat's home was an effort to intimidate a Trump critic.

items.title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game
items.description: The game continued after the incident. The American Conference said the decision was made before his death was known.

items.title: Personal attacks fire up debate before Brazil's run-off vote
items.description: The race heats up just days before the run-off between the left-wing incumbent and his right-wing challenger.

items.title: Deadly fire at Canada military base moved a kilometre 'in 30 to 60 seconds'
items.description: The blaze that killed four men and injured dozens of others spread with alarming speed, accounts suggest.

items.title: Possible wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane likely to be trees, say researchers
items.description: Researchers travelled to a remote Pacific Island to confirm whether an object first spotted on satellite imagery in 2020 solved the mystery of the pilot's disappearance.

items.title: Catalonia's former rebel president can return to Spain, court rules
items.description: The court upholds a decision to lift an arrest warrant for Carles Puigdemont linked to the independence bid he led in 2017.

items.title: Italy plans tougher security measures after violent protests
items.description: The government crackdown comes after protests over rising costs broke out into violent clashes.

items.title: Trump says suspension of Russia sanctions is to keep peace negotiations going
items.description: The US president blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect.

items.title: Bangladesh says it was not informed of its citizens' execution by Saudi Arabia
items.description: Saudi Arabia said it executed two Bangladeshis last week for committing an "indecent act" in a mosque.
